1.why: 29 is the only odd value among 26/28/32, but a parity singleton is a weak tell and could equally be a slip-distractor.

2.why: 4.5% is the only value carrying a decimal among three whole-number percents, the classic lone-computed-value tell.

3.why: Numerators 3,5,6,7 over a common 12; nothing separates 5/12 from 7/12, so this is an interior pick.

4.why: 17/25 is the only value not expressible as a simple fifth or a small numerator, so it looks like the computed one, but that is thin.

5.why: 16 = 6 + 10 makes it look derived (likely a distractor), leaving 13 as the lone odd base value.

6.why: 69.5 is an order-of-magnitude outlier and 26.75/34.25 straddle 29.5 nearly symmetrically, so 29.5 reads as the central value.

7.why: 2/15 is exactly the product of two other options (2/3 x 1/5), the standard independent-probability key with its own factors as distractors.

8.why: The set is two pairs 10 apart (30/40, 74/84); nothing picks a member, so this is essentially a coin flip on the larger pair.

9.why: A fully crossed 2x2 of {3,7} over {10,13} - every option is equally legal without the stem, so this item is clean.

10.why: 4/16 is the lone non-reduced-looking value and 5/16 is its complement partner's mate; 11/16 is the interior complement, but the set is nearly clean.

11.why: All four are binomial coefficients; 210 is the only multiple of 10, a weak round-number tell that could as easily mark a distractor.

12.why: 43.75% and 56.25% are the two computed sixteenths against round 25%/75%; the complement step usually lands on 43.75%, but the pair is symmetric.

13.why: 71, 74, 77 form an arithmetic run of step 3 with 104 as an outlier, and 74 is the median of that run.

14.why: 7/15 and 8/15 are a complement pair around a half; 8/15 is the larger, but nothing in the set decides it.

15.why: 4, 5 and 20 share an LCD of 20 while 5/12 is alien; 7/20 is the only value that needs that LCD to produce, so it reads as computed.

16.why: 20 and 60 are round multiples of 10 and 12 is a common factor value; 27 is the lone odd, non-round value.

17.why: 6, 9, 11, 14 has no run or function structure; 9 is the only perfect square, which is a very weak reason.

18.why: 1/2 is the lone round value written outside the eighths family and so likely a lure; among 3/8, 5/8, 7/8 nothing separates them.

19.why: 98/125 is the exact complement of 27/125 = (3/5)^3, so it is the more-derived member of the derived pair.

20.why: 1/2, 2/3, 3/4, 5/6 are four clean unrelated fractions with no run, product or odd-one-out - a clean item.

21.why: 3, 9 and 24 are all multiples of 3 (and 9 = 3^2), leaving 11 as the only value outside the distractor family.

22.why: Two complement pairs over 36 (15+21, 10+26) with no reduction or run tell; 21/36 is an interior pick.

23.why: In twentieths the set is 7, 8, 9, 10 - an arithmetic run with no single median; 9/20 is one of the two unreduced, computed-looking members.

24.why: 4/25 = (2/5)^2 and 21/25 is its complement; the complement is the more-derived value with 2/5 and 3/5 as given-looking lures.
